unique_answer_preserved_primary: Let the small square side be u. The subdivided quadrant contains a3-by3 array, hence its side3u. The other three unsubdivided squares share matching full quadrant sides and each have area9u^2. The whole outer square side6u, area36u^2. Seven of the nine unit squares and exactly one of the three larger squares are grey. Grey area=(7+9)u^2=16u^2, fraction16/36=4/9, uniquely D. Equal object counting would instead give(7+1)/(9+3)=8/12=2/3 (A). This is a square-count versus area-weight error: the actual side3-to1 distinction remains visible. The question asks a grey area fraction, not how many painted outlines or marks exist.
human_semantics_task_specific: The wording defines grey by unchanged interior fill. Open red strokes stay on existing edges only, without enclosing any new region, adding cuts, painting faces, or turning a white cell grey. Each of12 marks corresponds to exactly one actual square object. Small/large dimensions and every original seam remain visible, so humans can reject equal-area weighting and uniquely obtain4/9.
